description: Calculate moments, solve principle-of-moments balance problems, and analyse gear ratios.
content_html:
What Is a Moment?

A moment is the turning effect of a force about a fixed point called a pivot (or fulcrum). The moment depends on both the size of the force and how far it acts from the pivot, measured perpendicularly:

$$\text{moment (N m)} = \text{force (N)} \times \text{perpendicular distance from the pivot (m)}$$

Perpendicular distance is the shortest (right-angle) distance from the line of action of the force to the pivot. Using a longer perpendicular distance — by pushing further from the pivot — produces a larger moment for the same force. This is why it is easier to undo a bolt with a longer spanner than a short one.

Key Fact

Moment (N m) = force (N) × perpendicular distance from pivot (m). The unit of moment is the newton metre (N m). The perpendicular distance must be in metres. Increasing the distance from the pivot increases the moment.

A mechanic applies a force of 40 N at a perpendicular distance of 0.30 m from a pivot. Calculate the moment of the force.

Step 1: Write the equation. Moment = force × perpendicular distance.

Step 2: Substitute values. Moment = 40 × 0.30 = 12 N m.

The moment is 12 N m. If the mechanic moved their hand further from the pivot — say to 0.45 m — the moment would increase to 40 × 0.45 = 18 N m, making it easier to turn the bolt.

The Principle of Moments

When an object is in equilibrium (balanced and not rotating), the total clockwise moment about the pivot equals the total anticlockwise moment about the pivot. This is the principle of moments:

$$\text{sum of clockwise moments} = \text{sum of anticlockwise moments}$$

This is the basis for understanding seesaws, levers, cranes and many other real-world systems. The principle also allows us to calculate an unknown force or distance when a system is balanced.

A seesaw is balanced on a pivot at its centre. A child of weight 360 N sits 1.5 m to the left of the pivot. Where must an adult of weight 600 N sit on the right side to balance the seesaw?

Step 1: Calculate the anticlockwise moment (child on left). Moment = 360 × 1.5 = 540 N m (anticlockwise).

Step 2: Apply the principle of moments. Clockwise moment = 540 N m. So: 600 × d = 540.

Step 3: Rearrange. d = 540 ÷ 600 = 0.90 m from the pivot. The adult must sit 0.90 m to the right of the pivot.

Key Fact

Principle of moments: sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments (for an object in equilibrium). Use this to find an unknown force or distance in balance problems: find the known moment, then rearrange to find the unknown.

Levers

A lever is a rigid bar that rotates about a pivot. Levers act as force multipliers: by applying a small force at a large distance from the pivot, you can generate a large moment and so move a larger load at a smaller distance. A crowbar is a classic example — a small downward force applied near the end of a long crowbar creates a large upward force at the other end, close to the pivot.

The relationship comes directly from the principle of moments. If \(F_1 \times d_1 = F_2 \times d_2\) and \(d_1 > d_2\), then \(F_2 > F_1\). The lever amplifies force but you must move your end a greater distance to do so — the total work done on each side is the same (energy is conserved).

Gears

Gears are toothed wheels that mesh together to transmit rotation. When a small gear drives a large gear, the large gear rotates more slowly but with a greater turning force (moment). When a large gear drives a small gear, the small gear rotates faster but with a smaller turning force. The gear ratio determines how the rotation speed and moment change:

$$\text{gear ratio} = \frac{\text{number of teeth on driven gear}}{\text{number of teeth on driving gear}}$$

A gear ratio greater than 1 means the driven gear rotates more slowly but has a greater moment (force multiplication). A ratio less than 1 means the driven gear rotates faster but with less moment (speed multiplication). This is exactly why a bicycle has gears: lower gears (high ratio) make it easier to cycle uphill, while higher gears (low ratio) allow higher speeds on flat ground.

A driving gear has 15 teeth and meshes with a driven gear that has 60 teeth. The driving gear rotates at 200 revolutions per minute (rpm). Calculate: (a) the gear ratio, and (b) the rotation speed of the driven gear.

(a) Gear ratio = 60 ÷ 15 = 4. The driven gear has four times as many teeth as the driving gear.

(b) Speed of driven gear = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 rpm. The driven gear rotates more slowly by a factor of 4. In exchange, it exerts four times the moment of the driving gear.
exam_tip_html: In moment calculations, always check the distance is the perpendicular distance from the line of action to the pivot, and that it is in metres. For principle-of-moments balance problems, set up the equation clockwise = anticlockwise, calculate the known moment first, then rearrange for the unknown. Show all working even if it seems obvious — method marks are awarded at each step. For gear questions, the gear ratio is driven ÷ driving. A ratio >1 means slower speed and greater moment; ratio <1 means faster speed and smaller moment.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Moment (N m) = force (N) × perpendicular distance from pivot (m). A larger distance from the pivot gives a larger moment for the same force.
  • Principle of moments (equilibrium): sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments. Used to find unknown forces or distances in balance problems.
  • Levers amplify force at the expense of distance moved. Gears transmit rotation: a gear ratio >1 (large driven gear) gives more moment but slower rotation; ratio <1 gives less moment but faster rotation.

practice_questions.text: Calculate the moment produced by a force of 25 N acting at a perpendicular distance of 0.60 m from a pivot.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: Moment = force × perpendicular distance; moment = 25 × 0.60 = 15 N m; units stated.
Secure: Correct calculation with unit omitted or one minor error.
Developing: Equation recalled but values inverted or units incorrect.
Emerging: Numbers multiplied but no equation stated and no units.
One mark for: for an object in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a pivot equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.

practice_questions.text: A beam is balanced on a pivot. A force of 120 N acts 0.50 m to the left of the pivot. Calculate the force needed at 0.30 m to the right of the pivot to keep the beam balanced.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: Anticlockwise moment = 120 × 0.50 = 60 N m; applies principle of moments: F × 0.30 = 60; F = 60 ÷ 0.30 = 200 N. Units throughout; equilibrium condition explicitly stated.
Secure: Correct method with one arithmetic error; result follows from working.
Developing: Clockwise moment calculated correctly; rearrangement to find F attempted but incomplete.
Emerging: Identifies principle of moments but cannot set up the equation.

practice_questions.text: A driving gear has 20 teeth and a driven gear has 80 teeth. The driving gear rotates at 300 rpm. Calculate the rotation speed of the driven gear and state whether its turning force is greater or smaller than the driving gear.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: Gear ratio = 80 ÷ 20 = 4; driven gear speed = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 rpm; states that the driven gear has a greater turning force (moment) because the ratio >1.
Secure: Speed calculated correctly; turning force comparison correct but not explained.
Developing: Gear ratio correct; speed calculation attempted but error.
Emerging: Identifies that the larger gear rotates more slowly but cannot calculate the speed.

practice_questions.text: Explain how a lever can be used to lift a heavy object with a small force, using the principle of moments in your answer.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: A lever pivots about a fulcrum; applying a small force at a large perpendicular distance from the pivot creates a large moment (moment = F × d); by the principle of moments, this large moment can balance and lift a heavy load positioned close to the pivot (which has a smaller moment arm), so the effort force needed is much less than the load.
Secure: Identifies force multiplication; links to moment equation and principle of moments.
Developing: States levers multiply force with reference to pivot; does not link to moments equation.
Emerging: States levers make it easier to lift objects with no scientific explanation.

practice_questions.text: Describe the practical investigation that could be carried out to verify the principle of moments using a metre ruler, pivot and hanging masses.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: Describes balancing a metre ruler on a pivot at the centre; hanging known masses at measured distances on both sides; measuring the perpendicular distance from each mass to the pivot; calculating clockwise and anticlockwise moments (moment = weight × distance, where weight = mass × g); showing that clockwise moments total equals anticlockwise moments total when balanced; repeating with different masses/distances to confirm the principle. Identifies control variables (pivot position fixed); describes how to reduce uncertainty (use several masses, precise measurement of distances).
Secure: Most steps correct; moment calculation included; conclusion linked to principle of moments.
Developing: Describes balancing masses on a ruler; mentions moments but calculation or conclusion incomplete.
Emerging: General description of a balance activity with limited scientific content.

knowledge_checks.q: A force of 30 N acts at 0.4 m from a pivot. What is the moment?
A driving gear has 10 teeth and a driven gear has 50 teeth. What is the gear ratio?
For a balanced object, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of _____ moments.
Moment = force × perpendicular _____ from the pivot.
Match each gear ratio outcome to what it means:
right: Driven gear is slower but has greater turning force
Driven gear is faster but has smaller turning force
Driven gear spins at the same speed as the driving gear

flashcard_questions.q: What is the equation for the moment of a force?
flashcard_questions.a: Moment (N m) = force (N) × perpendicular distance from pivot (m).

flashcard_questions.q: What are the units of moment?

flashcard_questions.a: The fixed point about which an object rotates. Also called a fulcrum.
Clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments when a body is in equilibrium.

flashcard_questions.q: A force of 50 N acts 0.8 m from a pivot. What is the moment?
How does a lever act as a force multiplier?
flashcard_questions.a: A small force applied far from the pivot creates a large moment to balance a heavy load close to the pivot.

flashcard_questions.q: A driving gear with 20 teeth meshes with a driven gear of 60 teeth. What is the gear ratio?
If a gear ratio is greater than 1, how does the driven gear differ from the driving gear?
flashcard_questions.a: Driven gear rotates more slowly but exerts a greater turning force.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a longer spanner make it easier to tighten a nut?
flashcard_questions.a: Greater perpendicular distance gives a larger moment for the same applied force.
A state with no net force and no net moment — the object remains stationary and does not rotate.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must the distance in a moment calculation be perpendicular to the force?
flashcard_questions.a: Only the perpendicular component of distance contributes to the turning effect.

glossary_terms.definition: The turning effect of a force about a pivot. Moment (N m) = force (N) × perpendicular distance from the pivot (m).
The fixed point about which an object can rotate. Also called a fulcrum.
A state in which there is no net moment and no net force on an object, so it remains stationary and does not rotate.
For a body in equilibrium, the sum of all clockwise moments about a pivot equals the sum of all anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.
A rigid bar that pivots on a fixed point (the fulcrum), used to transmit and amplify forces or rotational effects.
Interlocking toothed wheels that transmit rotational forces. The ratio of the number of teeth determines how force and rotation speed are changed.
